Someone who arrives late joins the imam at once, then stands and completes what he missed after the imam's salaam. Many masjids have a separate women's entrance and prayer area.

Wudu is done at the taps in the washing area, usually beside the toilets, with clean clothes and a phone on silent for the prayer. The qibla is the direction of the Kaaba in Makkah, and the mihrab in the wall often shows it.

lessons.culture: Jumu'ah on Friday replaces Dhuhr and is prayed in congregation after the khutbah. Many men in Casablanca and Rabat wear a white djellaba for it, and during the khutbah everyone listens in silence. After the prayer people greet each other with جُمُعَةٌ مُبَارَكَة, and many families eat couscous together on Friday.

lessons.culture: In Morocco the traditional Qur'an school is called المسيد and its teacher الفقيه. Today many masjids in Casablanca and Rabat also run evening halaqat for adults and children, often after Maghrib, where each student recites from memory to the teacher. The mushaf is handled with clean hands and kept off the floor.

challenge.title: A Visit to the Masjid
challenge.instructions: Write and act out a conversation of at least 10 lines at the masjid. Ask about the next prayer and the iqamah, find the wudu area and the shoe rack, ask where the qibla is, put your phone on silent, and say what you do when you are late. Use at least 8 phrases from Unit 17.
required_elements: A question about the next prayer or the time of the adhan or iqamah, with فوقتاش or شنو.
A question about the entrance or the wudu area, with فين.
A request about the shoe rack, a prayer rug or the qibla.
A polite request or answer about the phone with عافاك or شكرا.
A missed rak'ah explained with فاتتني and the closing تَقَبَّلَ اللهُ with its reply مِنَّا وَمِنْكُمْ.
